minutes.headline: Superintendent signals schools want to keep the ACE program and central offices at Turkey Hill, shrinking the town hall project.
minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Municipal Building Design Committee interviewed new Superintendent Dr. Fortuna, who said the ACE program must stay collocated with the director of special services and that the superintendent's office does not need to be collocated with the town manager — a reversal of the prior superintendent's stated need that had driven significant square footage into the Ritter/town hall renovation plan. The committee treated this as a major finding that could shrink its project scope, discussed reduced need for a single consolidated town hall given growing online town services, set two Brooks House tour dates with the facilities director, and scheduled its next meeting for October 20th to get the town manager's input on collocation needs.

what_happened.line: The new superintendent told the committee the ACE program must stay with the director of special services and her office need not sit with the town manager, a reversal that could shrink the town hall project.
The committee treated that reversal as a likely major cut to the square footage the prior superintendent's collocation request had built into the plan.
Two Brooks House tour dates were set with the facilities director, Wednesday at noon and the following Tuesday evening.
The next meeting was set for October 20th to get the town manager's input on whether town offices still need to be under one roof.

A member suggested the town would likely pay the full cost of any central office or ACE space even inside a school project, citing the middle school greenhouse as a precedent the state did not fund; this was raised as a concern, not established.

why_it_matters: A smaller school-space requirement could shrink the size and cost of the town administrative building project residents will eventually vote on.
